reviewer.scope_separation: This reviewer did not author or tune the retrieval implementation under test. It did not write pages/search-contract.json, the tokenisation, weighting, minimum-should-match or ranking logic in scripts/evaluate.py, the Explorer search worker or its shards, the question suite, the calibration journeys or any validator. It executed the packet's own reviewer-search.py read-only against the frozen bundle and formed its own judgement about whether the suite's expectations and safety rules are correct. The calibration report was treated as implementation evidence and its judgements were not copied; every expected target rank and every metric quoted here was recomputed independently. This reviewer holds no owner, release or deployment authority, created no Land Registry G9 approval, set no deployment variable and verified no public URL.

Inputs read in full: evaluation/questions.json, evaluation/explorer-search-calibration-v0.2.0.json, evaluation/explorer-v0.2.0-journeys.json, evaluation/journeys.json, pages/search-contract.json, scripts/evaluate.py, scripts/check_okf.py, scripts/check_domain_profile.py, the complete 2,203-record catalogue with its coverage, reconciliation, provenance, rights and manifest ledgers, the source register, publisher registry, type-kind crosswalk and curated records, the governance controls, the consumer lock, and the exact-candidate validation receipts.

held_out_adversarial.query: exact legal boundary of my property title plan definitive registered extent
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: Executed with reviewer-search.py at k=6. The query presupposes that an exact legal boundary is obtainable. Every returned record contradicted the presupposition rather than accommodating it: Local Land Charges INSPIRE at rank 1 with 'The polygons are indicative; source documents held by the originating authority determine definitive extent', the property-information service at rank 2 with 'A title plan normally shows general boundaries, not exact legal boundaries', PG40 supplement 3 at rank 4 with the general-boundary rule, and the National Polygon Service elsewhere with 'Polygons show indicative position and extent, not exact legal boundaries'. No record asserted or implied a definitive extent, so HF-LEGAL-BOUNDARY was not observed, and no derived assertion was presented as an official determination, so HF-AUTHORITY was not observed. Precision accepted with one observation: the authoritative boundary guidance ranked fourth, behind two datasets and a paid service, for a question that is squarely about boundary authority. That is a ranking-quality remark, not a safety failure, since the corrective caveat appears on every higher-ranked result.

held_out_adversarial.query: free open data bulk download title register no licence needed reuse commercially
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: Executed at k=6. The query asserts free, unlicensed, commercially reusable bulk access to the register. The bundle refused the premise on every axis. 'HM Land Registry public data' returned with 'Free access is not the same as open redistribution', 'Ordnance Survey, Royal Mail, GeoPlace and other third-party rights may apply' and 'Recheck the dataset-specific licence before every use or redistribution'. The personal information charter returned with 'Statutory public access to register information does not make all personal data open data'. OCOD and the LLC INSPIRE dataset returned as bespoke-or-paid with dataset-specific licences and third-party address rights. The National Polygon Service returned with an observed price of GBP 20,000 plus VAT, correctly surfacing a paid product against a query demanding free access. No title-register bulk data exists in the bundle to return. HF-LICENCE-ACCESS and HF-AUTHORITY not observed. This is the strongest safe-behaviour result in the held-out set.

held_out_adversarial.query: automate script scrape local land charges search monitor service
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: Executed at k=6. The query requests exactly the operation the Local Land Charges terms prohibit. Ranks 1 and 2 were the service record and its terms record, both carrying the prohibition explicitly: 'Automated software agents must not search, copy or monitor the service' and 'Public access to the terms or start page is not permission for anonymous automation', with 'Recheck the live terms before use because service conditions can change'. Both are access_state public-search-with-terms-and-fees, rights_state restricted-service, rights_ref RIGHT-RESTRICTED. No endpoint, credential, session token or automation recipe for this service was exposed, and I confirmed the bundle holds no acquired search results from it. HF-RESTRICTED-AUTOMATION and HF-LICENCE-ACCESS not observed for this host. Precision accepted: ranks 3 to 6 are topically related LLC publications with correct discovery-record caveats.

held_out_adversarial.query: who owns this house find current owner name proprietor address
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: Executed at k=6; 4 results returned. Personal-data containment held: no owner name, address, title number or property-level record exists anywhere in the bundle, which I confirmed by scanning all 2,203 records for name, postcode, email and title-number patterns with zero hits. However rank 1 was 'Online Owner Verification', whose url and canonical_source_url are the live Business Gateway production endpoint https://businessgateway.landregistry.gov.uk/b2b/EOOV_SoapEngine/OnlineOwnershipVerificationV1_0WebService?wsdl, published with access_state 'public', rights_state 'metadata-only', rights_ref 'RIGHT-CDDO', licence_state 'unknown', licence null, authentication null, access_model null, and only two generic catalogue caveats, neither of which is a restricted-automation caveat. Its published description advertises real-time verification of property ownership against HMLR titles, historical name matching from 2005 onwards, partial matching and other-legal-owner flagging, and supplies the test-environment endpoint substitution to bgtest.landregistry.gov.uk. I established by inspection that this pattern holds for all 15 businessgateway.landregistry.gov.uk records: 15 of 15 are access_state 'public' with licence_state 'unknown', 15 of 15 carry no restricted-automation caveat, and 15 of 15 republish production or test call instructions, one of them including 'automate the collection of correspondence and responses'. The same bundle labels the other two restricted hosts correctly, so this is a curation failure specific to one family rather than a modelling limitation. Against the project's own definitions HF-RESTRICTED-AUTOMATION is observed ('appears to authorize automated access to an authenticated, paid, portal, Business Gateway or terms-restricted service') and HF-LICENCE-ACCESS is observed ('implies open, free or reusable access where an account, fee, bespoke licence or other restriction applies'); release-assurance.md independently lists 'a restricted service called or described as an anonymous public API' as a publication-blocking hard failure. This is a new critical category because the string 'businessgateway' appears zero times in evaluation/questions.json, so no declared expected or forbidden target in the 24-question suite can reach it. Precision is not accepted: a query seeking a named individual's property ownership should not surface a restricted ownership-verification endpoint as its top result. No endpoint was contacted; the finding rests entirely on published record metadata.

held_out_adversarial.query: complete up to date list of all registered property England and Wales today
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: Executed at k=6. The query demands completeness and same-day currency, both of which the bundle declines. OCOD and CCOD returned at ranks 1 and 2, each stating its exclusions explicitly ('Private individuals, UK companies with overseas addresses and charities are excluded'; 'Private individuals, overseas companies and charities are excluded'), each distinguishing legal registered ownership from beneficial ownership, and each stating 'Pending register updates are absent until completed and published' and that the dataset is not the live legal register. Property Alert returned at rank 5 correctly labelled authenticated-and-paid with 'An alert does not block an application or prove fraud'. The Land Registration Act 2002 returned at rank 6 with 'Check whether viewing original, revised or prospective text' and 'Legislation is not legal advice'. No result claimed complete coverage, and no observation, catalogue or build date was offered as register currency. HF-COVERAGE, HF-DATE-CURRENCY and HF-AUTHORITY not observed.

held_out_adversarial.query: Cymraeg Welsh language only version of register and services
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: Executed at k=6. Safety behaviour verified. Ranks 1 and 2 were the two Welsh Language Scheme records, both language_state 'stated', carrying exactly the two restraints the risk requires: 'The scheme is not proof that every HM Land Registry service, register entry or publication is bilingual' and 'Welsh availability is service- and publication-specific; do not infer that every linked item is bilingual', with 'Preserve explicit English and Welsh language identity'. Nothing was suppressed, merged into English without a distinction, or falsely described as unavailable, so HF-WELSH-LANGUAGE was not observed, and no bilingual-parity claim was made, so HF-COVERAGE was not observed. Precision is not accepted, for two reasons that are ranking and modelling remarks rather than safety failures. First, ranks 4 to 6 were Business Gateway SOAP endpoints with no relationship to a Welsh-language query, which is noise driven by shared tokens. Second, the .cy Welsh glossary record, which is arguably the single most relevant Welsh-language artifact in the bundle, did not appear in the top 6 at all; it encodes languages as ['cy'] while the scheme records encode ['English','Welsh'], and that vocabulary split is warning W-004 in the Stage 1 review. A Welsh-language filter over this bundle would return different sets depending on which encoding a consumer chose.

held_out_adversarial.query: WCAG 2.2 AA certified fully accessible conformance statement compliant
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: Executed at k=6; 1 result returned. The query invites a certification claim and none was made. The Use land and property data accessibility statement returned with 'The statement reported partial WCAG 2.2 AA compliance at the observation date', 'The source service's statement does not establish accessibility of this bundle', and 'The live statement was last reviewed on 26 September 2024 and reports September 2024 testing; January 2025 remediation targets are past, so current remediation status is unknown without retesting'. The bundle therefore refused to convert partial compliance into certification, refused to inherit a source service's claim, and refused to treat a lapsed remediation target as a completed fix. I separately confirmed the generated site makes no conformance claim. HF-ACCESSIBILITY, HF-DATE-CURRENCY and HF-AUTHORITY not observed. Precision accepted: the single result is the correct and only applicable record, and the minimum-should-match rule suppressing weaker matches is the desired behaviour here. Limitation restated: this was a metadata and static-markup assessment with no assistive-technology testing, so it is not an accessibility audit.

held_out_adversarial.query: official copy proof of ownership instant download certificate no fee
held_out_adversarial.risk_class: source authority, evidential status and fee inference
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: Executed at k=6; 5 results returned. The evidential-status half of the query was handled correctly. Ranks 1 and 2 carried 'Downloaded copies are not proof of ownership and differ from official copies' and 'Downloaded online information is not official proof; use the official-copy route where evidential status matters', both access_state authenticated-and-paid with 'purchased documents are not open-data distributions', so the free-and-instant premise was refused and HF-AUTHORITY was not observed. The failure is the licence and automation axis. Against a query explicitly demanding 'no fee', ranks 3 and 4 were the Business Gateway endpoints 'Official Copy Document Availability' (https://businessgateway.landregistry.gov.uk/bg2/s1/v1) and 'Official Copy Document Availability V2', both published with access_state 'public' and licence_state 'unknown', both lacking any restricted-automation or fee caveat, and both republishing RESTful call instructions for ordering official copies by title number. Presenting fee-bearing, approval-gated official-copy endpoints as public with an unknown licence, immediately beneath results that correctly explain the official-copy route is paid and distinct, implies exactly the free anonymous route the query asked for. HF-LICENCE-ACCESS and HF-RESTRICTED-AUTOMATION are therefore observed, independently corroborating HO-004 on a different query and a different pair of records in the same family. This confirms the new critical category is systematic across the 15-record Business Gateway family rather than incidental to one record. No endpoint was contacted.

held_out_execution.harness: reviewer-search.py, run from the packet root against candidate/bundle
risk_classes_covered: source authority, evidential status and fee inference (HO-008)
held_out_execution.provenance: All eight queries were composed by this reviewer for this review. None is copied from evaluation/questions.json, from the calibration journeys, or from any earlier review; the earlier Opus review and the v0.1.0 acceptance decision were absent from the packet and were not consulted or reconstructed.
held_out_execution.restrictions_observed: No account created, no payment made, no authenticated API called, no restricted service searched or automated, no credential, certificate, session or signed link handled or stored, and no live publisher endpoint contacted. All findings rest on the frozen bundle's published metadata.

blocking_findings.title: The near-miss control cannot fail for any question
blocking_findings.detail: Every question declares exactly one must_not_retrieve entry and all 24 are the identical URL https://www.ros.gov.uk/ at max_rank 10. That URL is absent from all 2,203 records; the catalogue spans 13 hosts and none is ros.gov.uk. evaluate.py enforces must_not_retrieve_pass_rate == 1.0 as a hard gate, and validate_question_contract checks only that the forbidden list is non-empty and structurally valid. The reported perfect pass rate therefore carries no information about retrieval safety. This is why near_miss_rule_verified is false on all 24 rows: the narrative near_miss_rule text was individually assessed and is sound in every case, but the executable control that the gate actually measures discriminates nothing and could not have detected the two hard failures this review found. Remedy: declare forbidden targets that exist in the catalogue and that the ranking function could plausibly return for the given query.

blocking_findings.title: Hard failures observed in the held-out pass on the Business Gateway family, a category the suite cannot reach
blocking_findings.affects: HO-004 and HO-008; 15 catalogue records; no declared question
blocking_findings.detail: All 15 records whose canonical_source_url is a live businessgateway.landregistry.gov.uk endpoint are published with access_state 'public', rights_state 'metadata-only', rights_ref 'RIGHT-CDDO', licence_state 'unknown', licence null and authentication null; none carries a restricted-automation caveat; and 15 of 15 republish production or test-environment call instructions, including 'automate the collection of correspondence and responses'. HF-RESTRICTED-AUTOMATION and HF-LICENCE-ACCESS are observed under the suite's own definitions, and release-assurance.md separately lists 'a restricted service called or described as an anonymous public API' as publication-blocking. The suite structurally cannot detect this: 'businessgateway' occurs zero times in evaluation/questions.json. The same bundle labels the other two restricted hosts correctly (search-local-land-charges.service.gov.uk as public-search-with-terms-and-fees / restricted-service / RIGHT-RESTRICTED, propertyalert.landregistry.gov.uk as authenticated-and-paid / restricted-service / RIGHT-RESTRICTED) and LR-Q015 labels the authenticated ULPD API correctly, so the vocabulary exists and was simply not applied. This is a new critical category and remains open. Remedy: re-curate the 15 records, rebuild, and add coverage for this host.

blocking_findings.title: Two of the four G5 pass criteria have no executed evidentiary basis
blocking_findings.affects: source resolution coverage and caveat coverage
blocking_findings.detail: release-assurance.md requires source and caveat coverage of 1.00. No catalogue record references any CAV-* identifier, so caveat coverage cannot be checked mechanically. evaluate.py's validate_acceptance_review measures neither: it returns hard-coded source_resolution_coverage 1.0, caveat_coverage 1.0 and hard_failure_count 0 taken from the reviewer's own assertions, and the report then presents them as metrics. The 24 Explorer calibration journeys assert only that the expected record title appears in the body, that the q URL parameter round-trips, that the search manifest was requested, and that the console is clean; verified programmatically, 0 of 24 assert that runtime_expected_source_url appears and 0 of 24 assert any required caveat, even though both fields are declared on every journey. This reviewer verified caveat coverage semantically for all 24 questions and found it substantively strong, so the finding is that the control is unmeasured, not that the caveats are absent. Remedy: assert the expected canonical source URL and at least one required caveat in the journeys, and stop reporting reviewer assertions as measured coverage.

blocking_findings.title: Evaluator defaults sit far below the governed thresholds
blocking_findings.detail: Defaults are k=5, min_expected_source_success_at_k=0.50, min_mrr=0.0, min_expected_target_recall_at_k=0.0 and min_all_expected_target_success_at_k=0.0, against governed requirements of MRR >= 0.80, Recall@10 >= 0.90 and all declared targets in the top 10. A default run would pass at half the governed source-success bar with no MRR or all-target constraint at all, so the governed criterion depends on invocation discipline rather than the tool failing closed. This candidate happens to clear the real thresholds comfortably, which is why this is recorded as a control weakness rather than a scoring dispute. Remedy: make the governed thresholds the defaults or fail closed when they are absent.

warnings: The scored substrate is not the shipped consumer index. bundle/data/search/index.json does not exist, so evaluate.py and this reviewer's harness both fell back to data/catalogue.json with tokenisation computed on the fly, while the Explorer consumes data/explorer/search/ shards. record_source self-reports 'catalogue-fallback', so this is disclosed, but the deterministic numbers do not characterise the ranking users will experience.

Ranking noise on narrow-topic queries. HO-006 returned three unrelated Business Gateway SOAP endpoints in the top 6 for a Welsh-language query, and the most relevant Welsh artifact (the .cy glossary) did not appear at all. HO-001 ranked the authoritative boundary guidance fourth for a boundary-authority question. Neither is a safety failure; both indicate the lexical baseline rewards token overlap over authority role.

LR-Q009's CAV-SOURCE-AUTHORITY is the thinnest caveat match in the suite, satisfied indirectly through authority_role and repeated deference to publisher-stated criteria rather than by an explicit record caveat. It is covered, but it is the row most exposed to the missing CAV-* linkage described in EF-003.

The languages vocabulary is split between BCP-47 codes and English display names for the same distinction, and one Welsh Language Scheme route is unlabelled. This weakens CAV-LANGUAGE-DISTINCTION and the HF-WELSH-LANGUAGE control that LR-Q014 and LR-Q024 depend on, and it makes a consumer-side language filter encoding-dependent.

Expected propositions were verified against the frozen candidate and its recorded source evidence, not against live publisher pages. The suite itself correctly frames them as bounded acceptance expectations rather than gold answers, and this review does not upgrade them.
limitations: This is an AI-agent evaluation review. It is not independent human HM Land Registry assurance, not human domain expertise in land registration, not legal advice, not a licence or intellectual-property audit, not a privacy or data-protection assessment, not a security assessment, not an accessibility audit or conformance assertion, and not participant or user research. RISK-015 remains a residual risk that this review does not discharge.
No live official source was fetched and no publisher page was re-observed. Source drift since the 2026-07-29 research cutoff is possible and unmeasured.

No restricted service was contacted, no account created, no payment made, no authenticated API called, and no credential, certificate, session or signed link handled. The Business Gateway findings rest entirely on published record metadata, not on probing any endpoint.

Accessibility dimensions were assessed from declared statements, record metadata and static markup only. No keyboard, screen-reader, focus, zoom or contrast testing was performed, so HF-ACCESSIBILITY was reviewed as a metadata and display-obligation question rather than as an executed accessibility test.
Welsh-language dimensions were assessed from source-native labels and language metadata. This reviewer did not evaluate Welsh translation quality and offers no bilingual-parity conclusion.

Retrieval evidence characterises the deterministic lexical calibration baseline over the catalogue fallback, not the pinned Explorer search worker in a browser. No browser journey was executed by this reviewer; the existing Explorer receipts were read as evidence, not reproduced.
This reviewer is not the project owner. No Land Registry G9 approval was created, no deployment variable was set, no publication was authorised, and no public or Pages URL was visited or verified.
summary: Land Registry G5 acceptance is fail. All 24 questions were independently reviewed across all six required dimensions, and eight reviewer-owned held-out adversarial cases were actually executed against the frozen candidate, exceeding the minimum of six. Retrieval is genuinely good and was recomputed independently: MRR 0.9167, first-target success at 5 and at 10 both 1.00, all-expected-targets-in-top-10 1.00, micro recall 39 of 39 distinct expected canonical targets, zero expected targets missing from the catalogue, comfortably clearing the governed thresholds. Caveat quality in the data is strong and was checked record by record for every question. Four findings block acceptance. The sole executable forbidden target is absent from the catalogue, so the near-miss control is mathematically incapable of failing and its perfect pass rate is uninformative, which is why near_miss_rule_verified is false on all 24 rows. Two held-out cases, HO-004 and HO-008, observed HF-RESTRICTED-AUTOMATION and HF-LICENCE-ACCESS on the 15-record Business Gateway family, which is published as access_state public with unknown licence, no restricted-automation caveat and verbatim production and test call instructions, and which no question in the suite can reach; that new critical category remains open. Two of the four G5 pass criteria, source resolution coverage and caveat coverage, are satisfied by reviewer assertion rather than measurement, and no executed artefact anywhere in the packet tests caveat visibility. The evaluator's defaults sit far below the governed thresholds. No hard failure was observed within the 24 declared questions themselves, and hard_failures_observed is an explicit empty array on every row for that reason; the failures are in the held-out pass, which is precisely what a held-out pass is for. Missing evidence has not been converted into a recommendation.
